ideas.name: CareCircle
ideas.pitch: One shared record for everyone caring for someone.

reasons: Aurora PostgreSQL is the primary back end, not an add-on

ideas.thesis: Caregiving is relational, transactional and access-controlled, so authorization belongs in the database — a key-value store cannot enforce it.
ideas.inversion: Permissions live in the database, not the UI.

track.ev_note: Identical $10,000 first prize to B2B; crowding unknown because the gallery is empty pre-announcement.

ideas.demo_moment: The hired aide's view blocked from a financial document — captioned 'blocked by the database, not the UI'.

scores.rationale: RLS-enforced multi-tenancy, ACID medication transactions, pgvector retrieval under the same policies.
Calm, accessible, role-scoped views purpose-built for stressed caregivers.
2.1 billion people will be 60+ by 2050; dual B2C and B2B monetization.
Fair-share visibility and the diaspora digest are fresh; family care records are not new.

ideas.name: Daily
ideas.thesis: A once-a-day global write spike with hot-key reads is the access pattern DynamoDB was built for, and the wrong shape for a relational engine.
ideas.inversion: The database is chosen by the access pattern, not the data model.

track.ev_note: Same $10,000 first prize; the architecture story is simpler to demo than to build.

ideas.demo_moment: A live counter of global predictions resolving at the daily cutoff.

scores.rationale: Single-table design with a considered partition key; less depth than a full RLS story.
Playful and clear, but a narrower surface.
Prediction games exist; the daily-global framing is the twist.

disqualified.name: PromptShelf

reasons: no required AWS database in the design — it stores prompts in a managed vector service
thin wrapper over an existing product category
